hypothesis: Every declared standard path has a reference end state accurate far beyond the integrators under test: closed forms on constant-curvature charts and a 34-digit extrapolated integration on the saddle, torus and gaussian bump, whose ciw-authored integrator agrees with mpmath's own Taylor-series integrator within its error estimate, and below it by the factor 2^p - 1 of its order p = 16 extrapolation.
input_data: Standard paths: plane (L=2.0), sphere (L=2.0), cylinder (L=3.0), saddle (L=1.5), torus (L=3.0), gaussian-bump (L=2.5), hyperbolic-plane (L=1.5), plane-polar (L=2.0), cylinder-polar (L=2.5)
Start states are the binary64 states used by the ciw integrators, converted exactly
mathematical_model: Great circle X(s) = cos(s/R) X0 + R sin(s/R) T0; helix and polar lines through the flat development; hyperbolic semicircles; transfer matrices cn_K, sn_K; otherwise the sympy-derived geodesic + Jacobi system integrated by Gragg-Bulirsch-Stoer in mpmath, and again by mpmath.odefun (Taylor series of degree 30 at 34 digits) as an integrator of another origin.
numerical_result: Largest ciw-vs-reference gap 6.38e-14; variable-curvature references saddle mpmath (self-estimate 1.44e-24), torus mpmath (self-estimate 4.35e-23), gaussian-bump mpmath (self-estimate 6.39e-22); Clairaut drift of the ciw end state 6.75e-14; mpmath.odefun (degree 30, 34 digits) differs from the Gragg-Bulirsch-Stoer references by saddle 1.8e-29, torus 6.8e-28, gaussian-bump 8.1e-27, 1.3e-05 to 1.6e-05 of their 10 vs 20 macro-step estimates; the observed orders log2(estimate / gap + 1), with the gap of the same macro-steps at 44 digits, are saddle 16.26, torus 15.96, gaussian-bump 16.28 against the nominal 16 of 8 modified-midpoint stages, so each estimate measures the error of the 10-step result, about 2^p - 1 times that of the retained 20-step one.
observation_model: Euclidean distance of embedded end points (chart distance on the hyperbolic plane) and max-abs difference of the 2x2 transfer matrix; between the two 34-digit integrations, the largest difference of the eight state components.

title: Build high-precision reference solutions for each surface.
uncertainty: The 34-digit references change by at most 6.39e-22 between 10 and 20 macro-steps; mpmath.odefun, which gives no estimate of its own, differs from them by at most 8.1e-27, inside every estimate, and the 34-digit end states carry measured rounding of at most 1.2e-32 (the same macro-steps at 44 digits), the uncertainty of each odefun gap; the reported reference end states and RK4 gaps are binary64, so each of those per-finding uncertainties is at least their binary64 rounding (about 1e-15); closed forms carry rounding only; the ciw Richardson error estimate is retained per path.
unresolved_assumptions: The 34-digit reference is an extrapolated integration, not a closed form; its error estimate is empirical

The Gragg-Bulirsch-Stoer integrator of the 34-digit reference is ciw-authored; wherever sympy and mpmath are installed its end states are checked against mpmath.odefun on the same sympy-derived equations, so the reference rests on equations (sympy) and a second integrator (mpmath) of origins other than ciw. mpmath supplies the arithmetic of both integrations, and neither gives a proved error bound: their agreement is empirical. The scipy DOP853 comparison integrates the ciw equations, so only its integrator is independent
